serviceTimeMs.how: mean = the Flask service (gunicorn)'s CPU per request at 1307 req/s net of idle: (44014 - 65 ms at rest) / 39211 requests = 1.1208 ms; shape (p95/median 1.0859/0.2887 ms) from the handler's own time

clientLinkLatencyMs.how: anchored: (measured median 1.310 ms - the model's median without it 2.108 ms at 1307 req/s) / 2, one way, at least 0

serviceTimeByLoad.how: the staircase's CPU per request net of idle (1.7054 ms at 50, 1.0087 ms at 755, 1.1202 ms at 1307 req/s), fitted never rising with rate and divided by the top rate's (1.1202 ms); flat outside the staircase

gcPauseMs.how: not modelled as a pause: each gunicorn worker collects on its own and stalls only its own request; the collections' CPU is in the CPU per request

writeServiceTimeMs.how: PostgreSQL's CPU per UPDATE with synchronous_commit off (0.2245 ms), shaped like its round trip (median 0.455, p95 4.331 ms)

readServiceTimeMs.how: PostgreSQL's CPU per SELECT (0.1753 ms, the pass's less its UPDATEs'), shaped like its round trip (median 0.424, p95 4.010 ms)

dbLinkLatencyMs.how: each way: the round trip the service measured less PostgreSQL's time, in two legs that keep its mean and variance (median 0.1123, p95 1.7454 ms)

dbCpuShare.how: PostgreSQL CPU per query at the top pass net of idle (0.1802 ms) / the model's mean time per query (35311 reads at 0.175 ms and 3900 writes without their flush at 0.224 ms: 0.180 ms)

commitFlushMs.how: PostgreSQL's own WAL flushes at 1307 req/s (pg_stat_wal): 3940 flushes of 1.090 ms on average, 0.99 commits per flush (the model: 1.00); shaped like the commit wait the service measured (p95/median 1.01, mean 1.285 ms)

serviceMemoryBaselineMb.how: at idle: the api-python container's working set (the highest reading in each pass) against req/s over 8 points (at rest and 7 passes, 50 to 1,307 req/s), by non-negative least squares: 326.5 MiB + 0.0013 MiB per req/s, largest error at and above the median rate 3%
